"Anyways, that's my annual suicide story for you. I tell these stories to hopefully remind others that you can make it too, and to remind myself just how far I've really come. 2012 took me 6 years to fully recover from. But I'm still here. I'm still breathing."

"At the age of 17, I didn't think I would make it to 20, let alone 27. Every day that I'm still here, whether to bring joy to those around me or as an act of defiance to those who hate me, is a day that could have been much different if I had just jumped once."

"Last night when Myth reminded me of the date by accident, I was just suddenly overcome with a very powerful feeling that brought me to tears. And that feeling was that I was still here. I'm still alive."
"But it became the spot. And this all started in June of 2012. A strange month of sadness and grief, trying to get over what I never had to begin with (hm, sounds familiar)."

"After that day, from then on, every time the depression just got to be too much, I went to that bridge. I sat, questioned, cried, and then left. I've said before that a jump from that bridge wouldn't kill me; this isn't the Golden Gate bridge by any stretch of the imagination. HTTPURL"

"I walked my bike over it, slowly. And I stared at the water the whole time. It was, and still is, the most painful walk I've ever taken in my life. What I didn't realize in that moment was that was the start of my suicidal thoughts that follow me to this day."

"I didn't, and I rode to the other side. As soon as I got to the other side, I burst into tears. I sat there and cried for a good while before I realized I had to go back home, and I had to cross the bridge again."

"But when I got to the bridge, I suddenly became very overwhelmed with emotions. I rode across it, and at one point, I stopped in the middle and stared over the water. I looked down. I wanted to do it."

"I finally had enough. I couldn't take it anymore, so I got on my bike and took a bike ride down to this fabled bridge. I don't think I went down there with suicide in mind, I just wanted to go there."

"On June 17th, the depression was once again at extremely severe levels and I was in a lot of pain. I contacted a friend and let's just say the conversation was the worst thing you could tell someone in that amount of pain."
"Then we get to this fucker. HTTPURL"

"The depression was so severe, that I remember one night it was so painful it felt like my heart was going to stop and I had to make something in sheer desperation just to get rid of the feeling. That thing I made was the video "Thick Woods" HTTPURL"
"It felt like it wasn't real. I was so detached from reality. Everything I knew about my life, who I was, my artistic identity, and my relationships, kinda crumbled to pieces in that month."

"All I remember of June of 2012 was this gaping hole in my chest that all of my emotions got swallowed into. There wasn't a single day in that month that was good. I wasn't happy once. I was miserable. I was alone. And it all felt very surreal."
